newsitem.title: USA: TVA says sets record for summer power demand.
newsitem.headline: TVA says sets record for summer power demand.

text.p: The Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) said Thursday that lingering hot and humid weather resulted in a record for summer power demand this past Tuesday.
Electricity demand soared Tuesday to a new high of 25,526 megawatts (MW) at 1800 EDT. The previous summer record of 25,496 MW was reached on July 13, 1995, the company said in a statement.
TVA's all-time peak was set during the winter season when it hit 26,670 MW on January 17, 1997.
The average temperature in the region at the time of the peak demand was 90 degrees F, the statement said. According to Weather Services Corp (WSC), humidity levels topped 70 percent.
Firm, peak power prices on a 16-hour schedule into TVA's system surged to as high as $85 per megawatt hour (MWh) on Tuesday before retreating to about $40 per MWh on Wednesday.

Forecasts in the Southeast are calling for the arrival of thunderstorms later Thursday, which are expected to cool temperatures to about two to four degrees F above normal through the weekend, WSC reported.
TVA provides power to large industries and 160 power distributors that serve about eight million consumers in seven southeastern states.
